headline: All majors underwater on the 200-day; whales dumping into Coinbase while funding stays positive and the crowd fears.
paragraphs: The regime is unambiguous: every major asset in the tape sits below its 200-day simple moving average, and none has a golden cross in prospect. Bitcoin is 49 percent off its 12-month high, Ethereum 60.6 percent, and Solana 70.4 percent. Bitcoin dominance stands at 56.2 percent, a stable perch, while total market cap edged up 0.09 percent on the day. This is a downtrend in place. The cross structure is uniform, six of seven majors without a bullish 50/200 setup, which removes any ambiguity about the direction the tape is pointing.

Momentum diverges from trend in ways worth naming. Bitcoin's RSI sits at 47.4, neutral, while its MACD has rolled below signal: that is a downtrend in motion, not resting. Ethereum reads higher at RSI 56.3 but also MACD below signal, a more complex picture, the momentum is less depressed but the trend confirmation has rolled over. Solana and XRP are even softer, with RSI at 42.7 and 42.9 respectively, both oversold territory on a 14-period horizon. Only two assets in the entire set show MACD above signal: BNB at RSI 48.3 and Doge at RSI 40.7. Neither reading is strong. The message from momentum is fatigue in the downtrend, not reversal; the tape is tired, not ready to turn.

Positioning tells a story of crowding in a weakening market. Bitcoin's perpetual funding is running at 0.0052 percent per 8-hour period (5.7 percent annualized), positive but shallow, traders are willing to hold longs but not paying hard for it. Ethereum is marginally richer at 0.0054 percent. Open interest on Bitcoin stands at 2.1 billion dollars with a long-to-short ratio of 2.26, meaning longs outnumber shorts by more than 2-to-1; that same ratio holds at 1.87 for Ethereum. These are crowded long books in a market moving lower. Solana flips the script: funding is negative (minus 0.8 percent annualized), shorts are being paid to hold, yet the long-to-short ratio is still 2.4, a major imbalance. Doge is the extreme: a 5.45-to-1 long bias with funding at 11 percent annualized, the hottest thermal read on the board. In a downtrend, extreme long bias is fragile; Doge's liquidation record over the past 23 hours shows 15 longs blown out against zero shorts, a one-way wipeout. The liquidation pattern in Bitcoin and Ethereum over 21 hours shows more shorts being rinsed than longs, a minor bullish tell, but the raw numbers are modest in size.

Whale behavior and spot flows sketch a picture of distribution into weakness. Over the past 48 hours, Bitcoin saw 62.6 million dollars flow onto Coinbase specifically, a net inflow to the exchange. The weekly trend on Bitcoin whale moves is volatile: outflows of 441 million last week, but three prior weeks showed net inflows of 445 million, 1.07 billion, and 740 thousand. This week's move onto an exchange is notable, whales are consolidating their holdings at a major venue. At the same time, Bitcoin ETF flows turned negative on August 14th at minus 56.2 million, with cumulative outflows of 385.2 million over the last five sessions and three consecutive down days. Ethereum ETF flows are positive but tepid, with only 5.9 million on August 13th and 46.6 million inflow over five sessions. Stablecoin float sits at 306.3 billion dollars, down 0.53 percent on the month, the dry powder is shrinking, not building. There is no pool of fresh capital waiting at the margin.

Sentiment is where the tape shows its real stress. The Fear and Greed Index reads 34, deep in fear territory, and has ranged between 25 and 34 over the past 30 days. That is a crowded floor with no relief, no rebound in sentiment. Yet the positioning and flow data suggest a different conversation: whales moving coins to exchanges, shorters being liquidated faster than longs, and funding remaining positive despite the downtrend. The disagreement between extreme fear and the ongoing bid for longs is a tension worth watching. It says the crowd is capitulating while someone, somewhere, is still buying the dips.

Watch for three things: a flip in whale direction, if the next weekly net turns positive and stays there, the distribution phase may be ending; a break in Bitcoin funding, which would signal shorts reasserting control; and any reclaim of the 200-day on Bitcoin, the simplest gate to a trend shift. None of those conditions are in place today. For now, the tape shows a downtrend with tired momentum, crowded longs, and whales feeding coins into exchange bids while the crowd sits in fear. That configuration does not persist without a spark.
